rationale: P identifies vehicle braking behaviour as the phenomenon that must be characterised to evaluate SG-3's prevention of unintended braking. H-3 explicitly establishes sudden stopping without an obstacle ahead as the hazardous event and supports the declared operational scope. Braking behaviour is therefore itself the subject of evaluation, not merely a control mechanism affecting another phenomenon. P does not incorporate sensing, computation, communication, failure-mitigation mechanisms, or their timing constraints.
determining_elements: "Braking behaviour of the ego vehicle" directly addresses the behaviour targeted by SG-3 and H-3.
"Whether braking occurs when no obstacle is present in front of the vehicle" captures the braking–environment relationship established by H-3.
The scope—straight-ahead driving on a less frequented urban road at 50 km/h, in good weather, without visible obstacles or vehicles ahead—matches H-3's operational situation.
P remains at the vehicle-behaviour level rather than including the mechanisms used to detect obstacles or prevent unintended braking.
